@graph.name: How to Hire a Senior SaaS Developer
@graph.description: A step-by-step guide to hiring a senior SaaS developer for your multi-tenant platform, subscription billing, and admin dashboard project.

step.name: Define your SaaS architecture requirements
step.text: Specify: B2B vs B2C, multi-tenancy model (RLS vs schema-per-tenant), billing model (flat/seat/usage), auth requirements (OAuth/SSO/SAML), and compliance needs (GDPR/HIPAA/SOC2).

step.name: Verify multi-tenancy and Stripe billing experience
step.text: Ask specifically: How do you implement tenant isolation? What is an idempotency key and why is it essential? Have you implemented dunning for failed payments? Have you done proration for mid-cycle plan changes?

step.name: Review production SaaS evidence
step.text: Ask for a live SaaS product they've built. Check: admin dashboard quality, Stripe billing flow (trial → paid → upgrade → cancel), and whether they can explain their multi-tenancy approach in detail.

step.name: Agree on MVP scope and milestones
step.text: Define MVP scope narrowly: auth + 1 core feature + Stripe checkout + basic admin panel. Avoid enterprise features (SSO, SCIM) in MVP. Use milestone-based contracts with written acceptance criteria per milestone.

step.name: Set up billing and tenancy architecture first
step.text: Build multi-tenancy and Stripe billing infrastructure before feature development. Retrofitting billing or tenancy into an existing codebase is 3–5× more expensive than building it correctly from day one.

step.name: Handover and documentation
step.text: Final deliverables: source code to your GitHub, Stripe webhook documentation, admin dashboard runbook, Alembic migration history, test suite with coverage report, and 60-minute walkthrough session.

mainEntity.name: What is multi-tenancy in SaaS and why does it matter?

acceptedAnswer.text: Multi-tenancy means multiple customers share one application instance with complete data isolation. It enables operational efficiency (one codebase, one deployment) and cost efficiency. Isolation is critical — one customer must never see another's data. PostgreSQL RLS is the gold standard for B2B SaaS.

mainEntity.name: How do you implement Stripe webhook idempotency?

acceptedAnswer.text: Store every processed Stripe event ID in a webhook_events table with a unique constraint. On receipt: check if event ID exists — if yes, return 200 immediately. Process inside a database transaction. Use idempotency keys on all Stripe API calls. Verify webhook signatures. A developer without idempotency has only done demo Stripe integration.

mainEntity.name: What is the best tech stack for building a SaaS application?

acceptedAnswer.text: 2026 SaaS stack: Next.js 14 + React + TypeScript (frontend), FastAPI or NestJS (backend), PostgreSQL + Redis (database), Auth0 or JWT (auth), Stripe (billing), Docker + Kubernetes on AWS/GCP (deployment), GitHub Actions (CI/CD), Sentry + Prometheus (monitoring).

mainEntity.name: What is the typical timeline for building a SaaS MVP?

acceptedAnswer.text: Basic MVP (auth + 1 feature + Stripe checkout + admin): 8–10 weeks, from $8,999. Standard MVP (multi-tenancy + billing + 3 features + admin dashboard): 10–14 weeks, from $12,999. Full platform (multi-tenancy + full Stripe lifecycle + usage metering + SSO): 16–24 weeks.
